covers: Steps to Reproduce 2-3
Expected: step 3 is refused

items.title: alice's order is still Submitted after bob's refused cancel
covers: Steps to Reproduce 4
Expected: after step 3, alice's order keeps the status it had
items.reason: The bug's damage was alice's order becoming Cancelled. A refusal status alone does not prove nothing was saved (the handler could cancel and then throw), so the persisted state is checked separately from alice's side.

items.title: bob, who has an order of his own, cancelling alice's order is refused with 404 and alice's order stays Submitted
covers: Expected: step 3 is refused
Expected: alice's order keeps the status it had
items.reason: The fix has two refusal paths: a caller with no buyer record and a caller whose buyer id differs from the order's. TC-BUG-54-02 covers the first; this case gives bob a buyer record so the buyer-id comparison itself is exercised. A shopper who has ordered before is the common real-world attacker.

items.title: bob's answer for alice's order is identical to his answer for an order number that does not exist
covers: Expected: the answer does not reveal whether that order exists
items.reason: The ticket requires the refusal not reveal whether the order exists; before the fix a missing order answered 500 while an existing one answered differently, which lets a caller enumerate order numbers. Comparing both answers in one run, as the same caller, is the only direct check; it needs alice's saved order, so it runs on the test stack.

items.title: A cancel request without a token is refused with 401 and alice's order stays Submitted
covers: Expected: a request without a token is still refused with 401
items.reason: The ticket keeps the anonymous 401 unchanged; the fix moves identity resolution into the handler, so a regression could let an anonymous request reach it. The functional host signs every request in automatically, so a real unauthenticated request is only possible on the test stack.

items.reason: TC-BUG-54-05 repeats the same no-orders bob request against alice's order and asserts the same 404 and empty body. Delete TC-BUG-54-02; TC-BUG-54-05 already catches an unauthorized cancellation or incorrect refusal response.

The existence comparison only uses bob with no buyer record. A handler that always refuses callers without buyer records but returns 500 for a missing order when the caller has a buyer record would pass every case while revealing existence. Extend this case to repeat the comparison after creating bob's own order, requiring matching 404 responses with empty bodies.

The existence-disclosure comparison uses only bob with no buyer record (matching story step 2), where the refusal can fire before the order lookup matters. A caller who has a buyer record (as in TC-04) is never compared for a missing order versus another shopper's order, which is the enumeration path most likely to diverge after a refactor. Consider adding that comparison to TC-04 or TC-05.
The expected result 'bob's own order B is unaffected (status Submitted)' is not stated in the story. It is harmless setup verification and can be dropped or kept as a precondition check.
